author: Bruno Mulé
title: Aroldis Chapman records 15th save
desc: Aroldis Chapman earned the save Thursday against the Yankees after allowing two hits and one walk over a scoreless ninth inning. He entered with Boston leading 6-3 and loaded the bases with two outs before retiring Ben Rice on a game-ending groundout.
impact: Chapman bounced back after allowing three runs without recording an out in his previous appearance. He now has 15 saves this season, tied for ninth-most in the majors.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Connelly Early strikes out season-high nine in win
desc: Connelly Early earned his seventh win Thursday against the Yankees, allowing two runs on five hits and one walk over six innings. He struck out a season-high nine batters and generated 17 swinging strikes. Early allowed one run on three hits in the first inning before limiting New York to a Jose Caballero solo homer over his final five frames.
impact: Early has completed six innings in consecutive starts after falling short of that mark in his first three outings of June. He owns a 3.59 ERA, 1.25 WHIP, and 88:32 K across 87.2 innings this season.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Cade Cavalli solid, but Nats bullpen turns it into a rout
desc: Cade Cavalli allowed two earned runs on five hits and one walk while striking out seven over six innings in Thursday's loss to the Phillies.
impact: After the outing, he owns a 4.00 ERA and 1.43 WHIP with a 4-4 record across 17 starts. He exited the game with a chance to earn the win, but the Nationals bullpen blew another lead in the series with the Phillies. Cavalli is slated to make his next start against Boston.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Jacob Young chips in, but Nats still drown in Philly
desc: Jacob Young went 1-for-3 in loss to the Phillies with two RBI and one stolen base.
impact: After Thursday's loss, Young is slashing .226/.274/.374 with eight homers, 30 RBI, 31 runs scored and eight steals across 77 games. Young is hitting just .125 over his last seven games.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Curtis Mead Homers in Loss
desc: Curtis Mead went 1-for-5 in Thursday's 10-5 loss to the Phillies with a solo home run, one run scored, one RBI and one strikeout.
impact: After the loss, Mead is slashing .223/.325/.427 through 66 games with 14 home runs, 39 RBI, 36 runs scored and three stolen bases. Mead has struggled over his last seven games, hitting just .154 with eight strikeouts.

author: Jesse Garcia
title: Dylan Crews swipes bag in three-hit loss to Phillies
desc: Dylan Crews went 3-for-4 in the loss to the Phillies with two runs scored, one stolen base and one strikeout.
impact: After Thursday's loss, Crews is batting .230 with five home runs, 17 RBI, 19 runs scored and three stolen bases across 32 games. Crews has been hot at the plate over his last seven games, hitting just.370 with eight runs scored.

author: Chase Davis
title: Carter Jensen swats solo shot in ugly loss to Rays
desc: Carter Jensen went 1-for-4 in Thursday's 13-2 loss to the Rays with a home run, one run scored and two RBI.
impact: Through 75 games, Jensen's slashing .244/.314/.437 with 11 home runs, 42 RBI, 39 runs scored, one stolen base, and a .325 wOBA. He extended his hit streak to 16 games with his ninth-inning homer, and he's batted leadoff each of the last 18 games against a right-handed starter.

author: Chase Davis
title: Seth Lugo shelled early as Rays rout Royals
desc: Seth Lugo allowed seven earned runs on seven hits and two walks while striking out three over five innings in Thursday's loss to the Rays.
impact: After Thursday's outing, Lugo now has a 4.18 ERA and 1.37 WHIP with a 3-5 record across 16 starts. He allowed seven hard hits, including three homers, and picked up eight whiffs on 90 pitches. Over his last four starts, Lugo has a 6.52 ERA, 1.45 WHIP, and 4.2 K/9 over 19.1 innings. He'll face the Rays again next time out.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Luis Robert Jr. (back) runs bases Thursday
desc: Luis Robert Jr. ran the bases on Thursday.
impact: Robert has been sidelined since late April with a lumbar spine disc herniation. He took batting practice in a cage on Tuesday, and Mets manager Carlos Mendoza said he looked normal and is pretty much symptom-free. Robert will continue to ramp up his running progression before beginning a minor league rehab assignment. Fantasy managers can expect him back at some point in the second half of the season.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Carlos Estevez (shoulder) to throw bullpen session Saturday
desc: Carlos Estevez is scheduled to throw a bullpen session on Saturday.
impact: Esteves, who has been recovering from a right rotator cuff strain since March 29, reportedly felt good following his Wednesday bullpen session. He has thrown two bullpens thus far and is scheduled for a third on Saturday. If all goes well, he could progress to facing live hitters next week. Fantasy managers should expect him to return in July.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Kris Bubic (elbow) to throw two innings at Triple-A Saturday
desc: Kris Bubic is scheduled to throw two innings with Triple-A Omaha on Sunday.
impact: Bubic resumed his rehab assignment on Wednesday, tossing a 1-2-3 inning. He is expected to work two innings in his next outing and should be activated from the injured list before the All-Star break.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Tanner Houck (elbow) begins light mound work
desc: Tanner Houck has begun light mound work.
impact: Houck underwent a hybrid reconstruction of his right UCL with flexor tendon repair last August and has officially begun light mound work. However, fantasy managers should not expect him to return until late in the season, as he still needs a couple of months to continue ramping up his throwing program before beginning a rehab assignment.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Matthew Boyd tosses 4.2 scoreless innings in return
desc: Matthew Boyd gave up no runs on four hits and four walks while striking out four across 4.2 innings in Thursday's 4-3 victory over the New York Mets.
impact: Boyd made his return to the starting rotation after being sidelined since May 6 with a left meniscus and shoulder injury, and did not allow an earned run across 76 pitches. While he struggled with command, issuing a season-high four walks, he was able to work out of jams when needed. He owns a 5.02 ERA and 1.36 WHIP with 35 strikeouts across 28.2 innings this season. His next scheduled start is on Wednesday against the San Diego Padres.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Steven Matz (ankle) placed on IL
desc: The Tampa Bay Rays placed Steven Matz on the 15-day injured list with a left ankle sprain.
impact: Matz reportedly entered his Tuesday outing against the Kansas City Royals with a sore ankle, and the injury worsened during the game, forcing him to the injured list after allowing five earned runs on six hits in just two innings of relief. He struggled mightily in June, posting a 14.54 ERA and 2.19 WHIP across 8.2 innings. In a corresponding move, Michael Grove was recalled from Triple-A Durham.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Cedric Mullins II steals base Thursday
desc: Cedric Mullins II went 2-for-4 with two runs scored and a stolen base in Thursday's 13-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals.
impact: Mullins has been generating some buzz in deeper leagues as a waiver wire pickup, and he continues to make a case for himself. Despite a rough season overall, he has been much better in June, slashing .259/.368/.414 with three home runs and three stolen bases this month.
